compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel Arc Pro B70 (Xe2/Battlemage class). fp16 capable, prefers vectorized loads, modest shared memory, SIMD16/32. No tensor cores like NVIDIA; relies on XMX-like matrix engines accessible through Triton tl.dot. Input shape 1x16x720x1280 -> output 1x32x720x1280 conv -> AvgPool 1x32x360x640.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Conv is small in_channels (16), 3x3, large spatial. tl.dot can be used by reshaping K*Cin into K dim. Fused conv+relu+avgpool reduces memory traffic significantly.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: tl.dot shape constraints on XPU; ensure M,N,K multiples of 16.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Dominated by reading 16-channel input and writing 32-channel pooled output. Fusing avgpool halves output traffic; fusing relu removes intermediate full tensor (32*720*1280*2B ~ 56MB).
memory_bandwidth.risk: Stride-2 pool read pattern; need to ensure coalesced loads.

register_pressure.notes: 16->32 channels small enough to hold weight tile in registers/shared. Tile per spatial block, channel-major accumulators.
register_pressure.risk: If we tile too large spatially, accumulator registers blow up.

nodes.notes: PROBLEM CLASS: 2D conv (stride1, 3x3, pad1) + bias + ReLU + AvgPool2d(k=2) on fp16. No quantization path (quantize=False, integer_forward=False). Output = AvgPool2(ReLU(Conv2D(x,W,b))). Shape: in [1,16,720,1280] fp16 -> conv [1,32,720,1280] -> pool [1,32,360,640]. DEPENDENCIES: each output pixel reduces over 3x3x16=144 fp16 mac; pool reduces 2x2 spatial. Can fuse conv+relu+pool to skip materializing full conv output. LAYOUT: NCHW contiguous fp16; weights [32,16,3,3]. ACCESS: input read multiple times due to 3x3 + pool (each input pixel feeds ~9 conv outputs and shares with pool neighbors). BOTTLENECK REGIMES: (1) Memory-bound full tensor materialization in eager -> winning by fusion. (2) Compute-bound for tl.dot path on small K=144. (3) Launch/overhead bound for very small tiles. KNOBS: tile size in H,W; whether to use tl.dot for [BLOCK_HW, 32] x [32, 144]; fuse pool inside kernel; precompute padded input or use masks; channels-last vs NCHW; vectorized fp16x2 loads. SKELETON: grid over (out_h_tile, out_w_tile, batch); each program loads weights once, iterates over kh,kw,cin accumulating fp32; add bias; relu; then 2x2 average inside kernel (compute 2x2 conv outputs and reduce) and store pooled result. CANDIDATES: A) Fused conv+relu+avgpool single Triton kernel, tile per output-pool-pixel block computing 2x2 conv values. B) Two-stage: Triton conv+relu storing full fp16, then small pool kernel (or torch). C) im2col+tl.dot matmul fused with bias/relu/pool.

action.description: Single Triton kernel that, for a tile of pooled output pixels (each covering 2x2 conv outputs), loads required 4x4+halo input region, performs 3x3 conv over 16 input channels into 32 output channels, applies bias+ReLU, then averages the 2x2 conv values to produce pooled output. Uses fp32 accumulation, fp16 storage. Weights kept in registers/SMEM. Grid over (pool_h_tile, pool_w_tile, oc_tile).
action.rationale: Fusing conv+relu+pool removes a 32*720*1280*2B intermediate (~56MB) round-trip, the largest gain available. Small Cin=16 makes inline conv viable without im2col.
action.title: Fused conv3x3 + bias + ReLU + AvgPool2d in one Triton kernel

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Avoid tl.dot complexity; use explicit MAC loops with vectorized loads. Good fit for Xe vector ALUs.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Scalar FMA chain; not using tl.dot; Arc Pro B70 prefers wider SIMD/XMX matmul.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input reloaded for every oc tile; weights reloaded for every spatial tile.

register_pressure.notes: 16 x loads + 4 accs per tile; manageable but limits BLOCK sizes.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT: does: single Triton kernel computes 3x3 conv over 16 in-channels per output channel, fuses bias+ReLU, then 2x2 average pool, writing fp16 output. bottleneck: likely bandwidth + redundant weight loads (scalar w loads per ic per program) and underutilized SIMD because each program covers only 1 out-channel per tile.
FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent: yes. Implementation matches intent of fusing conv+relu+pool with inline 3x3 convolution for small Cin.
UPDATE_BELIEF: Observed 0.36x vs eager (10.86ms vs 3.91ms), far below predicted 2.5x. Main suspects: (1) tile per (oc, h, w) means weights reloaded for every spatial tile; (2) only 1 oc per program reduces arithmetic intensity; (3) scalar weight loads & 16 input loads per pool pixel are not vectorized; (4) inner loop over C_IN=16 is small and prevents tl.dot use.
PERF_GAP: expected_vs_baseline_factor=2.5 vs observed≈0.36; reason: low arithmetic reuse and excessive global loads dominated; need to tile over OC (multiple oc per program) and/or use tl.dot via im2col-like layout.
next bet: child node n_fused_v2 to tile multiple output channels per program (BLOCK_OC>=4) and cache input region across OCs to amortize input loads.

action.description: Two Triton kernels: (1) conv3x3 + bias + ReLU producing full [1,32,720,1280] fp16 tensor; (2) AvgPool2d 2x2 kernel. Simpler to implement and validate; pool kernel is trivially memory-bound and cheap.
action.rationale: Lower implementation risk; isolates correctness of conv. Less fusion benefit but still avoids PyTorch overhead and quantizer no-op path.
action.title: Two-stage: fused conv+ReLU kernel, then separate AvgPool kernel

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Easier to use tl.dot or simple MAC loops independently.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Materializes full conv output (~56MB write + read for pool).
memory_bandwidth.risk: Larger DRAM traffic than fused variant.

nodes.notes: De-prioritized: n_fused already passed correctness at 0.36x; splitting reintroduces the 56MB intermediate that fusing was meant to remove. SELF_CHECK: alternative to n_fused family; kept open as low-priority fallback.

action.description: Reformulate conv as matmul: implicit im2col where each tile of output pixels gathers a [BLOCK_HW, 144] patch matrix and multiplies by [144, 32] weight matrix using tl.dot in fp16 with fp32 accumulation. Bias+ReLU+pool fused on the resulting tile.
action.rationale: Leverages XMX matrix engine via tl.dot; can be efficient if M,N,K alignment works. K=144 (multiple of 16), N=32 (multiple of 16) are friendly.
action.title: im2col + tl.dot GEMM-based conv, then fused ReLU+AvgPool

Load 4x4 input region per ic once, broadcast across BLOCK_OC weight values; use tl.dot or vectorized FMA across OC. Expect ~2-4x improvement by reducing redundant input/weight traffic. SELF_CHECK: mutually exclusive with n_fused_v2 because they restructure the same inner loop differently; only one will be chosen after evaluating n_fused_v2.

kernel_summary: Fuse a stride-1 3x3 conv (16->32 channels) with bias, ReLU, and 2x2 AvgPool on a [1,16,720,1280] fp16 tensor into a single (or two) Triton kernel(s) for Intel Arc Pro B70. The activation_quantizer is a no-op in the requested configuration (quantize_act=False), so the forward simplifies to AvgPool2(ReLU(Conv2D(x,W,b))). Dominant cost in eager mode is materializing the 56MB fp16 conv output; fusing pool eliminates that round-trip. Key constraints: NCHW contiguous fp16, weights [32,16,3,3] fp16, padding=1, fp32 accumulation for numerical fidelity, output [1,32,360,640].
open_questions: Does Triton on Intel XPU support tl.dot with fp16 inputs and fp32 accumulation for M/N/K including 32/144?
Is NCHW layout optimal on Xe2, or should we transpose to NHWC internally for vectorized channel loads?
What is the best spatial tile size (e.g., 4x16, 8x16 pooled pixels) given B70's register file and SLM size?
Are masked boundary loads (padding) cheap enough, or should we pre-pad the input tensor?
Does the activation_quantizer in this config truly act as identity, or does training-time scaling still apply?
How does bias dtype interact (likely fp16) and do we need fp32 bias add for accuracy tolerance?
What tolerance does the harness use (atol/rtol) for fp16 comparison, especially after avg pooling?
Is torch.xpu.synchronize required between kernel launches for accurate timing, and what is launch overhead on XPU?
